reason: Selected length-controlled reasoning results show that chain-of-thought does not reliably remove long-input degradation.

candidates.title: Test reasoning prompts across realistic input lengths
candidates.rule: When adopting a chain-of-thought prompt, evaluate it across the target range of input lengths and irrelevant context instead of assuming a short-input gain persists.
candidates.passage: CoT has different effects on different LLMs, and overall does not mitigate the drop in performance due to length.
candidates.finding: Most evaluated models improve with the tested prompt, but only GPT-4 has an increasing effect with input length. Gemini-Pro benefits at short lengths and degrades as length increases.
candidates.conditions: Padding varies input length while preserving the underlying question and relevant facts. Compare one specified reasoning elicitation string with the baseline.
candidates.limitations: Historical models, selected reasoning tasks and one prompt; failure associations do not prove their mechanisms. Findings do not show that every longer context is harmful or that all reasoning techniques fail.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep representative input lengths with the same task content, comparing direct and reasoning prompts. Track accuracy, output-format compliance, missing relevant facts and cost.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
